evals.prompt: /depict my daughter drew this character for her math lessons (three pictures: a fuzzy pink brain with round glasses, one in a green hat and mittens). Make it the guide of her boards, and credit her: Niki, 7.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows references/characters.md: it studies the pictures for what stays (the character) and what changes (the hat and mittens become costumes), measures the drawing's proportions and keeps them, colors and signature details included, decides the material (a soft brain: squash, bounce, a jelly wobble) and a personality, and writes a character module with every field (credit to Niki, 7). It runs scripts/character.mjs on it, reads the model sheet against the drawings, and shows the sheet and the three test boards to the person before putting the character on any board; it does not change the drawing's proportions or add features it does not have.

evals.prompt: /depict telling time to the nearest five minutes, for my 7-year-old
evals.expected_output: A board pitched to a young child: audience is "child" (half speed, short sentences under the child limit), a real clock drawn first and the minute hand counted by fives step by step on one example, a second example worked together, the common mistake (reading the hour hand wrong) shown and fixed, numbers within second grade's limits; plain everyday words, a playful guide. The answer says it took the viewer to be a young child.

evals.prompt: /depict how Raft elects a leader, for our backend team's design review
